item.title: One killed after Riyadh airport hit again, a day after deadly strike killed 12
item.description: The strike on King Khalid International Airport, the deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade, marked a major escalation in the war between Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis and the kingdom.

item.title: U.S. embassy urges "extreme caution" in Saudi airports after Houthi strikes kill several people
item.description: he conflict between Iran-backed Houthi militias and Saudi Arabia escalated over the weekend, with one American among 13 killed in strikes.

item.title: Hurricane Simon lashes Mexico's Pacific coast, pounds resorts and towns
item.description: Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 hurricane as it barreled toward Mexico's Pacific coast.

item.title: Trump administration ordered to cancel taxpayer-funded TV ads
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security tapped $20 million in taxpayer money for the ads, which the White House has defended as public service announcements.

item.title: Thousands still without power in Florida and Alabama as Isaias moves north
item.description: The storm, which hit as a Category 2 hurricane near Destin, Florida, has been linked to at least four deaths.

item.title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles in continued weapons tests
item.description: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were fired from an area around the North Korean capital of Pyongyang.

item.title: The real story behind Winnie the Pooh, born in the shadow of WWI
item.description: When soldiers of World War I traveled to Europe to fight, they would bring real animals meant to lift their spirits. One of them was an orphaned black bear from Canada. Tina Kraus explains how the cub inspired Winnie the Pooh, now 100 years old.

item.title: As high diesel prices hit Great Plains, some considering all options in midterms
item.description: Republicans have dominated elections in Great Plains states for a generation. But with the midterms fast approaching, Ed O'Keefe reports that some voters in Iowa now say they're considering all of their options.

item.title: Yemen's Houthis target King Khalid airport in Saudi Arabia again
item.description: Tensions flared in the Middle East following attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi Arabia. Leigh Kiniry reports.

item.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine "energy ceasefire" after criticizing Zelenskyy
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia alone is responsible for the war in Ukraine, after President Trump said he should be replaced.

item.title: Pope Leo to undergo surgery after nodular lesion found in lung, Vatican says
item.description: The American pope has no previously known health problems and is known to be physically active

item.title: Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire, Russia later strikes Ukraine
item.description: President Trump announced that he struck an energy ceasefire with Ukraine and Russia. Hours later, the Russians hit a neighborhood in the Ukrainian city of Kharkiv, including a power plant. It follows new criticism for the president's diesel deal with Russia. Taurean Small reports from the White House.

item.title: Pope Leo announces medical update
item.description: Pope Leo XIV, 71, said he will have surgery this week to remove a nodule in his lung. Chris Livesay has the latest in Rome.

item.title: Tropical Storm Rachel devastates homes in California: "We've never seen anything like this"
item.description: Tropical Storm Rachel caused devastation along the waterfront in Long Beach, California. Akiko Fujita reports and Grant Gilmore has the forecast.

item.title: A look at Hurricane Isaias damage after unleashing flooding, tornadoes
item.description: The first hurricane of the 2026 Atlantic season roared into Florida late Friday, unleashing destructive winds, extensive flooding and spinning up tornadoes across the Southeast. Jason Allen reports on the damage.

item.title: Jon Batiste says he's an introvert. Now, he's making "social music."
item.description: Jon Batiste, a Grammy-, Emmy- and Oscar-winning musician, considers himself deeply introverted. But he hasn't let that stop him from bringing people together with music.

item.title: 60 Minutes Transcript: Secret Service confronts rise in threats
item.description: The Secret Service warns of a sharp rise in threat levels in recent years both from within the U.S. and from outside the country. The agency is also developing its ability to defend against drones.

item.title: Secret Service developing offensive, defensive drone capabilities to confront threats | 60 Minutes
item.description: The Secret Service warns of a sharp rise in threat levels in recent years both from within the U.S. and from outside the country. The agency is also developing its ability to defend against drones.

item.title: Jon Batiste: The 60 Minutes Interview
item.description: Jon Batiste didn't set out to be a musician, but took up piano at his mother's urging. It's worked out. He now plays in sold-out venues around the world, bringing people together through music.

item.title: Some Israeli settlers use sheep to push Palestinians from West Bank homes
item.description: West Bank conflict has biblical roots, with Jewish and Arab populations fighting over ancestral land. But with all of today's high-tech warcraft, settlers fight using sticks and stones and sheep.

item.title: The Israeli settlers behind West Bank conflict with Palestinians | 60 Minutes
item.description: Israeli settlers, some of them violent, are using sheep farms as part of efforts to take over some West Bank land. They're clashing with Palestinians and also facing off against Israeli peace activists.

item.title: Drone swarms are a problem Secret Service says they have not solved yet
item.description: Secret Service Director Sean Curran and Deputy Director Matthew Quinn say they're dealing with an unprecedented number of threats and working on how best to handle attacks from drones.

item.title: 0/11/2026: In the Line of Fire; Lost Sheep; Jon Batiste
item.description: First, an inside look at Secret Service operations. Then, reporting on West Bank settler violence. And, Jon Batiste: The 60 Minutes Interview.

item.title: Trevor Phillips on protests in Europe | 60 Minutes
item.description: Londoner and new 60 Minutes contributor, Trevor Phillips is keeping an eye on student protests in France. But France isn't alone in its troubles. Across Europe, Phillips says, political unrest threatens to change the way the continent lives.

item.title: 10/11: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Deadly Isaias barrels north; Tropical Storm Rachel remnants soak the West.

item.title: Man killed by tiger in England after entering enclosure at wildlife park
item.description: The incident occurred at the Yorkshire Wildlife Park near the city of Doncaster, police said.

item.title: Rep. Jeffries says Democrats are "on the verge of taking back control"
item.description: Jeffries campaigned in New Jersey and Pennsylvania and plans to campaign in Texas in the coming days to help Democratic candidates unseat Republican incumbents.

item.title: Gunman charged with killing officer, wounding another in West Philly
item.description: Eric Lewis faces several charges, including homicide of a law enforcement officer, in the shooting death of 40-year-old Shane Seiber.

item.title: Iran calls U.S. response "insufficient" amid stalled talks to end the war
item.description: After Saudi Arabia said Iran's Houthi allies carried out another strike at Riyadh's airport, Iran called the U.S. effort to negotiate toward ending the war "insufficient."

item.title: OpenAI halts model release over safety concerns: "Didn't quite meet the bar"
item.description: OpenAI said it has chosen not to release its new GPT-6.1 Astra model due to concerns about safety, as industry leaders warn of the risks posed by ever-more-powerful AI technology.
